title: The data-science lifecycle
subtitle: Data science is a loop, not a line: ask, collect, clean, explore, model, check, deploy — and go round again.

what.title: What data science is
what.body: Data science extracts knowledge and decisions from data using statistics, programming and domain understanding. It sits between three skills: mathematics/statistics (what is true?), computing (how to do it at scale?) and the domain (is it meaningful?). Related terms: analytics describes the past, machine learning learns patterns to predict, big data means volume, velocity and variety beyond one machine.

loop.title: The lifecycle
loop.body: Typical stages (CRISP-DM style): business understanding → data collection → preparation → exploration → modeling → evaluation → deployment → monitoring. Results at any stage often send you back: poor evaluation means revisit features or collect more data.

Variables are numeric (discrete or continuous) or categorical (nominal, or ordinal if ordered). The type decides which summary and chart are allowed.

roles.title: Sources and tools
roles.body: Sources: databases, APIs, sensors/IoT, web scraping, surveys, logs. Typical tools: Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn), SQL, notebooks, visualisation libraries. Data engineers build pipelines; analysts explain; scientists model.

bias.title: Good questions and samples
bias.body: A vague goal (“improve sales”) becomes a measurable question (“which customers will churn in 30 days?”). Sampling matters: a random sample represents the population; convenience or self-selected samples are biased. More data does not fix a biased sample.
bias.steps: A shop has 400 customers; 60 churned last month. Churn rate: Predicting “no churn” for everyone is right 85 % of the time yet useless — accuracy alone misleads on imbalanced data.

lim.title: What data cannot tell you
lim.body: Correlation is not causation; past patterns may not hold; a model is only as good as its data (“garbage in, garbage out”). Randomised experiments (A/B tests) are how causal claims are earned.
